proofs.proof_tex:
By the cited Yang algorithm-equivalence result, Algorithm 1 returns an ancestral ordered grouping, and Definition 7 of that source makes this grouping a partition. More concretely, at each iteration Algorithm 1 assigns every selected substantive row to exactly one output group and then removes that row; hence no row can occur in two output groups, and termination assigns every row. The known map \(\ell\) is used in the observed-variable branch of the algorithm: a directly observed row that occurs in a mixed candidate group is fixed as its cogent center, whereas a row permitted to exchange the center role is retained in that group's candidate set. Thus label restriction can delete a candidate role but cannot duplicate a row. It follows that the sets \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) are pairwise disjoint.

By the definition of \(V_{\mathrm{fix}}\),
\[
V_{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G,\ell)=V\setminus\bigcup_{g=1}^kR_g.
\]
Disjointness therefore gives the asserted disjoint union
\[
V=\left(\bigsqcup_{g=1}^kR_g\right)\sqcup V_{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G,\ell).
\]
Consequently every \(u\in V\) lies either in a unique \(R_g\), in which case the first branch in the definition of \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}\) gives that unique \(g\), or in \(V_{\mathrm{fix}}\), in which case its value is \(\bot\). This proves totality and uniqueness of the group map.

Finally, a legal completion \(\omega=((r_h,c_h))_{h=1}^k\) selects exactly one cogent center \(r_g\in R_g\) in group \(g\). Hence, for \(u\in R_g\), the selected center is \(u\) exactly when \(r_g=u\); every other substantive row in that group has the mleaf role in that reconstruction. Algorithm 1 assigns rows outside all cogent candidate sets to singleton mleaf groups, and the definition of \(\Omega\) retains those labels as fixed singleton mleafs. Thus \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\) implies that \(u\) is an mleaf in every legal completion, as claimed.

Fix \(\omega\in\Omega(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), and abbreviate \(R=R(\omega)\), \(C=C(\omega)\), \(L=L(\omega)\), and \(H=H(\omega)\). The pivot and causal-order constraints in the definition of a legal choice give
\[
W_{r_gc_g}\ne0\quad(g\in[k]),\qquad
W_{r_gc_h}=0\quad(g<h).
\]
Therefore \(\Delta_\omega\) is invertible, and
\[
(Q_\omega)_{gg}=W_{r_gc_g}/W_{r_gc_g}=1,\qquad
(Q_\omega)_{gh}=0\quad(g<h).
\]
Thus \(Q_\omega\) is unit lower triangular and hence invertible.

Work first in the normalized source units \(\bar N_C=\Delta_\omega N_C\). In the row order \((R,L)\), the reconstructed substantive equations are
\[
X_R=A_\omega X_R+B^C_\omega N_H+\bar N_C,
\qquad
X_L=D_\omega X_R+B^L_\omega N_H.
\]
Because \(I-A_\omega=Q_\omega^{-1}\), their retained mixing matrix in the source order \((\bar N_C,N_H)\) is
\[
\overline W_\omega=
\begin{pmatrix}
Q_\omega&Q_\omega B^C_\omega\\
D_\omega Q_\omega&D_\omega Q_\omega B^C_\omega+B^L_\omega
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Each block now reduces directly from the reconstruction definitions:
\[
Q_\omega=W[R,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1},
\]
\[
Q_\omega B^C_\omega
=Q_\omega Q_\omega^{-1}W[R,H]
=W[R,H],
\]
\[
D_\omega Q_\omega
=W[L,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1}Q_\omega^{-1}Q_\omega
=W[L,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1},
\]
and
\[
D_\omega Q_\omega B^C_\omega+B^L_\omega
=D_\omega Q_\omega B^C_\omega+\bigl(W[L,H]-D_\omega Q_\omega B^C_\omega\bigr)
=W[L,H].
\]
Consequently
\[
\overline W_\omega=
\begin{pmatrix}
W[R,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1}&W[R,H]\\
W[L,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1}&W[L,H]
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Returning from \(\bar N_C\) to the original source units multiplies the selected mixing columns by \(\Delta_\omega\), so the retained representative is exactly \(W\). Equivalently, the normalized reconstruction represents the same column-scaling equivalence class as \(W\).

Since the inverse of a unit lower-triangular matrix is unit lower triangular, \(A_\omega=I-Q_\omega^{-1}\) is strictly lower triangular in group order. Thus the center submodel is acyclic. The remaining blocks have precisely the canonical types: \(D_\omega\) points from centers to mleafs, \(B^C_\omega\) and \(B^L_\omega\) load root latent sources, and mleafs have neither substantive children nor distinct structural noises. The pivot, label, acyclicity, and latent-confounder constraints are all part of membership in \(\Omega\); hence the reconstructed model is legal and canonical.

For scale invariance, let \(S\) be any invertible diagonal column-scaling matrix and put \(W'=WS\). With the induced relabeling of the chosen columns,
\[
\Delta'_\omega=\Delta_\omega S_C,\qquad
W'[R,C](\Delta'_\omega)^{-1}=W[R,C]\Delta_\omega^{-1}=Q_\omega.
\]
The same cancellation gives \(A'_\omega=A_\omega\) and \(D'_\omega=D_\omega\), while
\[
(B^C_\omega)'=B^C_\omega S_H,\qquad
(B^L_\omega)'=B^L_\omega S_H.
\]
The latter two changes merely rescale the independent latent sources. Thus the structural reconstruction and its observed law are invariant to independent nonzero column rescalings.

Fix a legal \(\omega\). In the substantive row order \((R(\omega),L(\omega))\), the coefficient matrix among substantive variables is
\[
G_\omega=\begin{pmatrix}A_\omega&0\\D_\omega&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The upper-right and lower-right blocks vanish because a canonical mleaf has no substantive children. Since \(I-A_\omega=Q_\omega^{-1}\), block multiplication gives
\[
(I-G_\omega)^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}(I-A_\omega)^{-1}&0\\D_\omega(I-A_\omega)^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}Q_\omega&0\\D_\omega Q_\omega&I\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Indeed, multiplying the last matrix by \(I-G_\omega=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}Q_\omega^{-1}&0\\-D_\omega&I\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) gives the identity block by block.

In an acyclic linear structural equation model, replacing the equation for \(u\) by an additive intervention of size \(t\) changes the substantive solution by \(t(I-G_\omega)^{-1}e_u\). Therefore the derivative with respect to \(t\), which is the labeled total-effect column, is the \(u\)-th column of \((I-G_\omega)^{-1}\). This derives the causal target from the structural equations; it does not define it from \(W\).

If \(u\in L(\omega)\), that column is the corresponding standard basis vector. Hence its diagonal entry is one and every off-diagonal entry is zero. By the observation-group partition, this covers both the fixed branch \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\) and the branch \(u\in R_g\) with \(r_g\ne u\).

If \(u=r_g\), the same column is the \(g\)-th column of \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}Q_\omega\\D_\omega Q_\omega\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The normalized-reconstruction identities give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}Q_\omega\\D_\omega Q_\omega\end{pmatrix}
=W[V,C(\omega)]\Delta_\omega^{-1}.
\]
Its \(g\)-th column is therefore \(W_{\bullet c_g}/W_{u c_g}\). The denominator is nonzero by the legal-pivot condition. Its \(u\)-entry is one, and its \(v\)-entry is \(W_{vc_g}/W_{uc_g}\). This proves every case in the displayed formula. The last expression uses only the pair \((r_g,c_g)=(u,c_g)\); choices in groups other than the unique group containing \(u\) do not occur. This proves the asserted locality.

Fix a tuple and labels satisfying the theorem. Separability identifies the retained mixing representative from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) up to column permutation and nonzero scaling. The normalized-reconstruction lemma shows that the formulas below are invariant under that indeterminacy. By the cited Yang algorithm-equivalence result, on \(\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) the minimum-edge legal reconstructions indexed by \(\Omega^\star\) are exactly the DOG representatives compatible with the recovered grouping and labels. The original model supplies at least one legal Algorithm-2 choice, so \(\Omega\) is nonempty; because it is finite, \(e^\star\) is attained and \(\Omega^\star\ne\varnothing\).

If \(v=u\), the local-effect theorem gives \(\tau_\omega(u\leftarrow u)=1\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega^\star\), so the image is \(\{1\}\). Suppose henceforth that \(v\ne u\). If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), the partition lemma and local-effect theorem give \(\tau_\omega(v\leftarrow u)=0\) for every minimum completion, so the image is \(\{0\}\).

Now let \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\). Split the minimum completions into
\[
\Omega_u^\star=\{\omega\in\Omega^\star:r_g=u\},
\qquad
\Omega_{\neg u}^\star=\{\omega\in\Omega^\star:r_g\ne u\}.
\]
For \(\omega\in\Omega_u^\star\), the projection definition implies \((u,c_g)\in P_g\), hence \(c_g\in L_u\), and the local formula gives
\[
\tau_\omega(v\leftarrow u)=\frac{W_{vc_g}}{W_{uc_g}}.
\]
Conversely, if \(c\in L_u\), then \((u,c)\in P_g\); by the definition of \(P_g\) there is an \(\omega_c\in\Omega^\star\) with \(\omega_{c,g}=(u,c)\), and the same formula attains \(W_{vc}/W_{uc}\). All such denominators are nonzero because they are legal pivots. Likewise, \(\Omega_{\neg u}^\star\ne\varnothing\) holds exactly when \(z_u=1\), and every member of this set has effect zero. Therefore
\[
\{\tau_\omega(v\leftarrow u):\omega\in\Omega^\star\}
=\left\{\frac{W_{vc}}{W_{uc}}:c\in L_u\right\}
\cup\bigl(\{0\}\text{ if }z_u=1\bigr),
\]
which is exactly the third branch of the defined functional \(S_{vu}\). This proves equality of the causal image and the observable recovery functional rather than imposing that equality by definition.

Since \(L_u\subseteq C_{\mathrm{src}}\) and \(|C_{\mathrm{src}}|=q\), the ratio set has at most \(q\) elements, and adjoining zero adds at most one. Thus \(|S_{vu}|\le q+1\). The converse arguments in the preceding paragraph supply an attaining minimum completion for each displayed ratio and, when present, for zero; the diagonal and fixed-mleaf branches are attained by any element of the nonempty finite argmin \(\Omega^\star\). If the image contains unequal values \(s\ne t\), choose the corresponding attaining completions \(\omega_s,\omega_t\). Their reconstructions are legal and minimum-edge. They have the same retained mixing matrix after the allowed source rescalings, and the removed one-hot measurement-error columns and their source laws can be appended identically. Choosing the correspondingly rescaled independent source laws therefore gives the same \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), while the local-effect formula gives unequal labeled effects. These are the required observationally equivalent countermodels.

Finally, the definition of \(\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) deletes, within each nonempty fixed canonical coefficient stratum, only proper algebraic exceptional loci from the Yang recovery and faithfulness-preservation argument. A proper real algebraic subset has Lebesgue measure zero in that stratum's free Euclidean coefficient coordinates, so the qualifier is relative Zariski generic and stratumwise Lebesgue-almost-everywhere. Separability concerns the source law and remains the separate stated assumption; it is not a Zariski property of \(\theta\). An exactly encoded rational input is a deterministic point and no probability assertion about it follows or is used.

The complete-image theorem reduces the question to equality of the finitely many values in the displayed definition of \(S_{vu}\). If \(v=u\), then \(S_{uu}=\{1\}\). If \(v\ne u\) and \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), then \(S_{vu}=\{0\}\). These prove the first two branches and their common values.

Suppose \(v\ne u\) and \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\). Every \(c\in L_u\) occurs as a legal pivot paired with center \(u\), so
\[
W_{uc}\ne0\qquad(c\in L_u).
\]
If \(L_u=\varnothing\), nonemptiness of the finite argmin \(\Omega^\star\) implies that some projected pair in \(P_g\) has center different from \(u\). Hence \(z_u=1\) and \(S_{vu}=\{0\}\).

If \(z_u=1\), zero belongs to \(S_{vu}\). The set is a singleton if and only if every ratio also equals zero. By the nonzero-denominator condition,
\[
\frac{W_{vc}}{W_{uc}}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
W_{vc}=0,
\]
so this is equivalent to \(W_{vc}=0\) for every \(c\in L_u\), and the common value is zero. This argument includes the empty \(L_u\) case vacuously.

It remains to consider \(z_u=0\) and nonempty \(L_u\). There is no adjoined zero, so singletonness is equivalent to equality of all ratios. For any \(c,d\in L_u\), both denominators are nonzero and
\[
\frac{W_{vc}}{W_{uc}}=\frac{W_{vd}}{W_{ud}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
W_{vc}W_{ud}-W_{vd}W_{uc}=0.
\]
Thus all ratios are equal if and only if every displayed \(2\times2\) minor vanishes. When they do, the common value is \(W_{vc}/W_{uc}\) for any \(c\in L_u\). The case analysis is exhaustive and proves both directions of every branch in the proposition.

We give an exact finite certificate. Introduce center, latent-loading, mleaf, and mleaf-loading blocks
\[
\Gamma=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\14&0&0\\14&11&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B^C=\begin{pmatrix}4&0\\10&16\\0&13\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
D=\begin{pmatrix}4&0&0\\9&18&0\\0&0&7\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B^L=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\\5&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Direct inversion gives
\[
Q=(I-\Gamma)^{-1}=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\14&1&0\\168&11&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Consequently, in source order \((N_0,N_1,N_2,H_0,H_1)\),
\[
\begin{pmatrix}Q&QB^C\\DQ&DQB^C+B^L\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&0&4&0\\
14&1&0&66&16\\
168&11&1&782&189\\
4&0&0&16&0\\
261&18&0&1224&288\\
1176&77&7&5479&1323
\end{pmatrix},
\]
which is exactly the benchmark mixing matrix.

The nonzero directed coefficients are
\[
c_0\to c_1,\ c_0\to c_2,\ c_1\to c_2,\quad
H_0\to c_0,\ H_0\to c_1,\ H_0\to l_2,\quad
H_1\to c_1, H_1\to c_2,
\]
\[
c_0\to l_0, c_0\to l_1, c_1\to l_1, c_2\to l_2.
\]
This graph is acyclic in the displayed order. Both \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) are roots and have at least two children; the \(l_i\) have no children and no distinct structural noise. Adding an independent one-hot measurement-error source for each measured row supplies the observation equations without changing the retained matrix. Hence the displayed model is canonical.

We next verify rank faithfulness exactly. Reorder the retained columns as \((H_0,H_1,N_0,N_1,N_2)\); the integer path matrix is
\[
\widehat W=
\begin{pmatrix}
4&0&1&0&0\\
66&16&14&1&0\\
782&189&168&11&1\\
16&0&4&0&0\\
1224&288&261&18&0\\
5479&1323&1176&77&7
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For the preceding graph, the ancestor and possible-parent sets in Yang et al.'s Assumption 3 are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
x&\operatorname{An}(x)&\operatorname{PP}(x)\\ \hline
c_0&\{H_0\}&\varnothing\\
c_1&\{H_0,H_1,c_0\}&\{c_0,l_0\}\\
c_2&\{H_0,H_1,c_0,c_1\}&\{c_0,c_1,l_0,l_1\}\\
l_0&\{H_0,c_0\}&\{c_0\}\\
l_1&\{H_0,H_1,c_0,c_1\}&\{c_0,c_1,l_0\}\\
l_2&\{H_0,H_1,c_0,c_1,c_2\}&\{c_0,c_1,c_2,l_0,l_1\}.
\end{array}
\]
For each admissible triple \((x,J,K)\), compute the rank of \(\widehat W[K\cup\{x\},J]\) by fraction-free integer elimination. Independently compute the minimum bottleneck size by enumerating the \(2^8\) subsets \(B\) of the eight graph vertices and taking the least \(|B|\) for which every directed path from \(J\) to \(K\cup\{x\}\) meets \(B\). Both operations use only integer arithmetic and finite Boolean path checks. The complete count certificate is
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|rrrrr}
x&\#\text{ tests}&0&1&2&3&4\\ \hline
c_0&2&1&1&0&0&0\\
c_1&32&4&16&12&0&0\\
c_2&256&16&78&122&40&0\\
l_0&8&2&6&0&0&0\\
l_1&128&8&50&70&0&0\\
l_2&1024&32&221&428&303&40
\end{array}
\]
where the entry in column \(s\) counts triples for which both the exact rank and the exact minimum bottleneck size equal \(s\). The row totals sum to
\[
2+32+256+8+128+1024=1450,
\]
which is the full set of distinct tests from both clauses of Assumption 3; the mleaf-clause tests are included because their allowed \(J\) and \(K\) are subsets of the corresponding displayed ancestor and possible-parent sets. There is no unmatched triple. This is precisely LV-SEM-ME rank faithfulness.

The rank-faithfulness verification meets the hypothesis of the cited Yang minimality criterion. The latent \(H_1\) has no mleaf child. The only mleaf child of \(H_0\) is \(l_2\), while \(c_0\) is another child of \(H_0\) and
\[
c_2\in\operatorname{An}(l_2)
\quad\text{but}\quad
c_2\notin\operatorname{An}(c_0).
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{An}(l_2)\nsubseteq\operatorname{An}(c_0)\), so the nonminimality witness required by that criterion does not exist. The benchmark is minimal.

It remains to enumerate its legal reconstructions. Let \(a_0,a_1\in\{0,1\}\) record the center switches \(c_i\mapsto l_i\) in the first two groups, let \(z\in\{0,1\}\) record \(c_2\mapsto l_2\), and let \(x,y\in\{0,1\}\) record the noise switches \(N_0\mapsto H_0\) and \(N_1\mapsto H_1\), respectively. Every candidate pivot is one of
\[
1,4,16\quad\text{in group zero},\qquad
1,16,18,288\quad\text{in group one},\qquad
1,7\quad\text{in group two},
\]
and is nonzero. The normalized center block is lower triangular for every choice. Exact substitution into the four reconstruction blocks also shows that each complementary latent column has at least two nonzero loadings, so all \(2^5=32\) choices are legal canonical reconstructions.

Counting nonzero entries after the same exact substitutions gives a value independent of \(a_0,a_1\):
\[
E(a_0,a_1,z,x,y)=12+x+z+(1-z)y.
\]
For completeness, the eight values indexed by \((x,y,z)\) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
(x,y,z)&000&001&010&011&100&101&110&111\\ \hline
E&12&13&13&13&13&14&14&14.
\end{array}
\]
Each entry occurs for all four values of \((a_0,a_1)\), giving four reconstructions with twelve edges, sixteen with thirteen, and twelve with fourteen. Therefore \(e^\star=12\), and equality holds exactly when \(x=y=z=0\). These four minimizers select all \(N_i\), select \(c_2\), and freely select \(c_i\) or \(l_i\) for \(i=0,1\).

The stated nonglobal choice has \((z,x,y)=(1,0,1)\), hence \(E=13\). Any change confined to group zero changes only \((a_0,x)\) and leaves the value at least thirteen. Any change confined to group one changes only \((a_1,y)\), and with \(z=1\) the value remains at least thirteen. A change confined to group two replaces \(z=1\) by \(z=0\) while \(y=1\), again giving thirteen. Simultaneously repairing the second noise and third center sets \(y=z=0\), yielding twelve. This proves the plateau and every asserted destructive check.

Assume the stated polynomial-time oracle \(\mathsf A_{\min}\). One unconstrained call returns
\[
e^\star=\min_{\omega\in\Omega}E(\omega)
\]
and an attaining completion. For each \(g\in[k]\) and each \((r,c)\in R_g\times K_g\), call the constrained oracle and denote its returned optimum by \(e_{g,r,c}\), taking its value to be \(+\infty\) on an infeasibility certificate. Since the constrained feasible set is a subset of \(\Omega\),
\[
e_{g,r,c}\ge e^\star.
\]
By the definition of the projection \(P_g\),
\[
(r,c)\in P_g
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
e_{g,r,c}=e^\star.
\]
The forward implication uses the minimum completion witnessing membership in \(P_g\); the reverse implication uses the completion returned by the constrained call. Retain that completion whenever equality holds. Thus the calls compute every \(P_g\) and one attaining global minimizer for each of its members.

The candidate products \(R_g\times K_g\) are disjoint subsets of \(V\times C_{\mathrm{src}}\), because the recovered row groups and source groups are pairwise disjoint. Therefore
\[
\sum_{g=1}^k|R_g||K_g|
=\left|\bigsqcup_{g=1}^k(R_g\times K_g)\right|
\le |V|\,|C_{\mathrm{src}}|=pq.
\]
Hence there are at most \(pq\) constrained calls.

From the retained tables, compute \(L_u\) by collecting the columns paired with row \(u\), and compute \(z_u\) by checking whether a retained pair in the unique group of \(u\) has another center; use the stipulated fixed-mleaf branch when the group map is \(\bot\). The complete-image formula then computes every \(S_{vu}\). For a fixed ordered pair \((v,u)\), at most \(q\) ratios are formed or compared, and equality can be checked without division by
\[
W_{vc}W_{ud}=W_{vd}W_{uc},
\]
together with the numerator-zero tests when zero is attainable. There are \(p^2\) ordered pairs, so this stage takes \(O(p^2q)\) rational operations in addition to reading the projection tables.

If the image is a singleton, the same comparisons return its value: one on the diagonal, zero on a zero-admitting singleton branch, and any retained ratio otherwise. If it is not a singleton, choose two unequal generated values. The constrained calls stored a minimum completion for each ratio-generating local pair and for every alternative-center pair generating zero. The two corresponding stored completions attain the unequal values by the local-effect theorem, hence are the promised countermodels. All denominators used are certified nonzero pivots. Because the oracle and every subsequent rational operation have polynomial bit time by hypothesis and exact rational arithmetic, the whole reduction has the claimed complexity.

On the stated subclass every substantive variable is directly observed and no substantive row can take an mleaf role. The observation-group partition and the known-label restriction therefore make each center-row candidate set a singleton, say \(R_g=\{u_g\}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{fix}}=\varnothing\). Consequently \(z_u=0\) for every \(u\), while \(L_u\) is exactly the set of retained source columns that can be assigned as the structural-noise column of the fixed center \(u\) in a minimum reconstruction.

For \(v\ne u\), the complete-image formula becomes
\[
S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)
=\left\{\frac{W_{vc}}{W_{uc}}:c\in L_u(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\right\},
\]
and \(S_{uu}=\{1\}\). Each denominator is a legal nonzero pivot. Normalizing a candidate column \(c\) so that its \(u\)-entry is one turns its \(v\)-entry into exactly \(W_{vc}/W_{uc}\). With no measurement-error rows or center exchanges, the remaining ambiguity is precisely the assignment of an observed structural-noise column versus a root-latent column in canonical latent-variable LiNGAM. Hence the displayed set is its normalized mixing-column effect set.

On the intersection of the two generic domains, the complete-image theorem says that the total effect is observationally identifiable exactly when this complete set is a singleton. The cited Tramontano theorem says that, for the same canonical latent-variable LiNGAM model with unknown graph, generic identification of that total effect is equivalent to their Theorem 3.3 graphical condition. The two equivalences concern the same observational equivalence class and the same intervention derivative. Therefore
\[
|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{Tramontano et al.'s unknown-graph criterion holds for the effect of \(u\) on \(v\)}.
\]
The singleton-minor corollary supplies the equivalent normalized-column equality test, completing the reduction.

added_lemmas.statement: For a canonical LV-SEM-ME satisfying Yang et al.'s LV-SEM-ME faithfulness and minimality conditions, Algorithm 1 returns its ancestral ordered grouping as a partition in causal group order, Algorithm 2 enumerates the legal ancestral-ordered-group reconstructions, and the minimum-edge output of Algorithm 2 is exactly its DOG equivalence class on the probability-one domain of Theorem 3.

source.locator: Definition 7, Algorithm 1, Algorithm 2, Theorem 3(2), and Proposition 7(2)

attestation.note: Checked directly against the cited definition, algorithms, theorem, and proposition in the published-source manuscript.

added_lemmas.statement: For a canonical LV-SEM-ME \(M\) satisfying LV-SEM-ME rank faithfulness, \(M\) is nonminimal if and only if there are a root latent variable \(H_i\) and an mleaf child \(Z_j\) such that \(\operatorname{An}(Z_j)\subseteq\operatorname{An}(V_a)\) for every other child \(V_a\) of \(H_i\).

attestation.note: Checked directly against Assumption 3 and Proposition 2; the source notes that its rank faithfulness implies conventional faithfulness.

added_lemmas.statement: In a canonical latent-variable LiNGAM with unknown graph, let \(u\) and \(v\) be observed variables and let \(\operatorname{de}_o(a)\) be the observed descendants of a node \(a\). The total effect of \(u\) on \(v\) is generically identifiable if and only if there is no latent node \(h\) such that \(\operatorname{de}_o(u)=\operatorname{de}_o(h)\) and \(v\in\operatorname{de}^{G\setminus u}_o(h)\), where \(G\setminus u\) deletes all arrows into \(u\).

attestation.note: Checked directly against Theorem 3.3 in the PMLR paper.

proposed.statement: For every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), the label-restricted recovered candidate sets are pairwise disjoint and \(V=(\bigsqcup_{g=1}^{k}R_g)\sqcup V_{\mathrm{fix}}(\mathcal G,\ell)\). Hence \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)\) is defined uniquely for every \(u\in V\). If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\), then \(u\) is the cogent center in a legal completion exactly when \(r_g=u\), and otherwise it is an mleaf in that group. If \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), then \(u\) is a fixed singleton mleaf in every legal completion.
proposed.justification: A total label-to-group map is necessary to bind the group index in every intervention-specific image and to separate switchable group members from fixed singleton mleafs.
proposed.gap: Yang et al. recover label-restricted AOG groups, but the effect layer requires the induced per-label partition and fixed-mleaf branch to be stated explicitly.
proposed.consumer: The partition makes every subsequent intervention-specific effect set a well-defined function of its displayed arguments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses Yang et al.'s published AOG and DOG recovery guarantee, which must be declared as a cited leaf.

proposed.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), every \((\theta,M,P_{\mathrm{obs}},W,\mathcal G(W,\ell))\in\mathfrak M_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{Yang}}(\mathbb R)\), and every \(u,v\in V\), the complete image of \(\tau_{\omega}(v\leftarrow u)\) over all minimum-edge DOG representatives is exactly \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) in \(\text{def:effect-image}\), and \(|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|\leq q+1\). For every \(s\in S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) there is an attaining \(\omega_s\in\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\); if the image is not a singleton, two such minimum completions furnish observationally equivalent countermodels with unequal labeled total effects. The qualifier is relative Zariski generic over each real canonical coefficient variety, equivalently Lebesgue-almost-everywhere in each stratum's free coefficient coordinates, while source-law separability remains a separate assumption; no probability claim is made for rational inputs.
proposed.justification: The exact set, not a selected representative, is the population object required for honest causal reporting under DOG equivalence.
proposed.gap: Salehkaleybar et al. project latent-variable LiNGAM ambiguity onto effects, but their admissible transformations omit measured-variable center changes and known measurement labels; Yang et al. give only a four-node robustness example.
proposed.consumer: A measurement-error analyst can distinguish a robust effect from a finite list of observationally indistinguishable alternatives and receive attaining models for sensitivity analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Equality between the minimum-edge reconstruction set and the published DOG class uses Yang et al.'s cited equivalence result.

proposed.statement: The instance \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\) is canonical, minimal, and LV-SEM-ME rank-faithful. Among its thirty-two legal reconstructions, \(e^{\star}=12\), and exactly four completions attain the optimum: each selects \(N_i\) as the structural noise, selects \(c_2\) as the third center, and independently selects \(c_i\) or \(l_i\) as the first two centers. The choice \(((c_0,N_0),(c_1,H_1),(l_2,N_2))\) has thirteen edges, every one-group change has at least thirteen edges, and a simultaneous repair of the second noise and third center attains twelve.
proposed.justification: The faithful plateau rules out strict coordinate descent and any additive per-group edge score before they can contaminate the main algorithm.
proposed.gap: Neither Yang et al.'s Cartesian enumeration nor adjacent equivalence-class enumeration papers isolate a faithful coupled-cancellation benchmark of this form.
proposed.consumer: Any proposed polynomial completion solver must recover this exact optimum and four-model plateau as its first destructive unit test.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact graph certificate proves rank faithfulness directly and invokes the published graphical criterion only for minimality.

proposed.statement: On the real subclass with no measured substantive variables and no mleaf rows, and for \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) reduces to the normalized mixing-column effect set of latent-variable LiNGAM. On this shared generic subclass, \(|S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)|=1\) if and only if the total effect of \(u\) on \(v\) satisfies Tramontano et al.'s unknown-graph criterion in Theorem 3.3.
proposed.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that the mixed-model image agrees with the complete published criterion when measurement error disappears.
proposed.gap: The proposition claims equivalence only on the shared no-measurement generic subclass and does not relabel the published lvLiNGAM theorem as new.
proposed.consumer: Existing lvLiNGAM users obtain a backward-compatible effect image while gaining the mixed-model extension when noisy measurements are introduced.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The final equivalence explicitly uses Tramontano et al.'s published unknown-graph total-effect theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact unrestricted complexity of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\), both unconstrained and with a prescribed pair, remains unclassified.
open_obligations.obstruction: The support counts of \(Q_\omega^{-1}\), \(D_\omega\), and \(B^L_\omega\) contain exact rational cancellations coupled across several groups. The faithful plateau proves that strict coordinate descent and an additive local edge score fail, but it is neither a hardness reduction nor a polynomial-size state representation.
open_obligations.attempted: The available routes were fraction-free ordered elimination with a rank signature, separation over feasible signatures, scalar dynamic programming, and exact cancellation gadgets. No polynomial bound on the signature space or separation oracle was derived, and no gadget reduction preserving the canonical, minimal, rank-faithful promise was completed.
open_obligations.partial_result: The exact oracle-to-image reduction is proved in \(\text{thm:projected-oracle-reduction}\), and \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{plat}}\) is an exact faithful witness that neither strict one-group descent nor an additive per-group edge score solves the general problem. A nontrivial polynomial restriction does close: if at most one group \(g_0\) has more than one legal local pair, then \(|\Omega|\le |R_{g_0}||K_{g_0}|\le pq\). Enumerating those pairs, rejecting illegal pivots, evaluating the four reconstruction blocks by fraction-free elimination, and taking the smallest exact support count solves both the unconstrained and prescribed-pair problems. For an input of bit length \(B\), every intermediate determinant has bit length polynomial in \(p+q+B\), so this enumeration is polynomial in the required bit model. What remains open is the unrestricted complexity classification when several groups interact through cancellation in \(Q_\omega^{-1}\), \(D_\omega\), and \(B^L_\omega\).
